lore: Public terminal at the edge of known space.
source_line: Figures: well-known public IAU / JPL-class values. Prose: Last Circuit.

home.here_lead: You are reading this on Earth. The rings are a stack of addresses drawn for this terminal. They are not a map tile and not a sky survey.

rings.label: Solar System
rings.note: One star and its worlds. Mostly empty space.

rings.label: Orion Arm
rings.note: The local spiral spur where the Sun sits. Thousands of light-years long.

rings.label: Milky Way
rings.note: Our galaxy. About 100,000 light-years across, as a round figure.

rings.label: Observable universe
rings.note: The region from which light has had time to reach us.

home.mission_text: Close three circuits: Mars, Saturn, and a black hole. The log marks each one. Sixty seconds is a dare, not a limit.

scaleStops.label: Human
scaleStops.cadet: A person is about 1.7 meters tall. Every other tick on this line is a length set next to that body.
scaleStops.analyst: Reference length 1.7 m. The scrubber is logarithmic. Equal steps are powers of ten, not equal meters.

scaleStops.label: Earth
scaleStops.cadet: Earth's equatorial diameter is about 12,756 km. A person disappears on this tick. The planet does not.
scaleStops.analyst: 12,756 km equatorial, the same round figure used on the Earth file. Mean diameter is a little smaller. The difference is invisible at this scale.

scaleStops.label: Sun
scaleStops.cadet: The Sun is about 1,392,000 km across, roughly a hundred Earths wide. Among stars it is ordinary.
scaleStops.analyst: Diameter about 1.392 million km. Radius over Earth-orbit radius is only about 0.005, which is why a true-scale drawing makes the Sun a small core inside a large empty ring.

scaleStops.label: Jupiter orbit
scaleStops.cadet: This tick is the width of Jupiter's path around the Sun, not the width of Jupiter. The planet is a speck on that circle.
scaleStops.analyst: About 10.4 AU across, twice the mean orbital radius of 5.20 AU. Do not read this tick as a planet diameter. The emptiness inside the circle is the point.

scaleStops.label: Heliopause
scaleStops.cadet: The heliopause is where the Sun's wind gives way to the gas between the stars. A Voyager craft crossed that region near 120 AU. It is not a wall. The distant comet cloud, if it is populated as expected, sits much farther out.
scaleStops.analyst: About 120 AU, the order of the Voyager crossings. The boundary is uneven and it moves. It is not the edge of the Sun's gravity. A round figure, not a surveyed curb.

scaleStops.label: Proxima Centauri
scaleStops.quantity: Distance to the nearest star beyond the Sun
scaleStops.cadet: Proxima Centauri is about 4.24 light-years away. The light you would see tonight left years ago.
scaleStops.analyst: 4.24 light-years, a rounded parallax figure. About 268,000 AU. The light-year is defined so that the number of years and the distance match for a straight trip at c.

scaleStops.label: Milky Way
scaleStops.quantity: Width of the stellar disk, round figure
scaleStops.cadet: Our galaxy's starry disk is on the order of 100,000 light-years across. The Sun sits in a spiral spur, far from the center.
scaleStops.analyst: 100,000 light-years is a round figure for the stellar disk. Published estimates of the exact stellar edge differ by a large fraction. Treat this as an order of magnitude, not a curb measurement. The dark-matter halo, if included, is wider still.

scaleStops.label: Observable universe
scaleStops.cadet: A common figure for the width of the observable universe is about 93 billion light-years. It is the region we can in principle see, not a fence, and not a claim that nothing exists beyond it.
scaleStops.analyst: About 93 billion light-years across. Model-dependent: the number uses an expansion history, not a tape. Reasonable model changes move it, but not by a silly factor. The last digit is not known. Order-of-magnitude language is the honest one.

blocks.title: Scientific figures
lines: Public-domain science and well-known IAU-class / JPL-class values, rewritten.
This project does not copy encyclopedia pages, textbooks, or agency prose.
Giant-planet moon totals are mid-2026 catalogue language and are marked as changeable.
No figure is given to twelve fake decimals.

blocks.title: Not in this terminal
lines: No agency insignia and no claim of agency affiliation.
No live network calls for science data.
Lines tagged LORE are framing. Lines tagged FACT are the science.

solar.caption_readable: FACT — Readable orbits squeeze the outer system so every world can share the frame. Sizes are enlarged. Angles are a diagram, not tonight's sky.
solar.caption_honest: FACT — space is mostly empty. Distances follow mean orbital size. Dots and the Sun's glow are still enlarged, or the inner worlds would vanish. Zoom out for Neptune and Pluto.
solar.webgl_note: WebGL did not start. The flat schematic is the circuit.
solar.a11y: Solar system schematic; select a planet from the list.
solar.decor: The dim point field is decoration, not a star catalogue.

delay.title: Light-delay switchboard
delay.fact: FACT — Radio in vacuum, at the speed of light. These are distances from the files divided by c. Not today's measured range.

compare.title: Compare bench
compare.fact: FACT — Ratios use the round figures in the local files. For the Sun, day means equatorial spin, not a sunrise.
